Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the trial credits — the team ran a pilot across two services last week and we need a clear line-item export to reconcile with our internal chargeback model. Two asks: 

1) Can you provide an itemized CSV that shows per-day, per-model token usage (prompt + completion), with model name and billed tokens for April 1–10? We need this to map to internal GL codes.

2) If we move to a 6-month commit, what does the per-token rebate schedule look like by tier? Specifically: what per-token price would apply at 0–5M, 5–25M, and 25M+ tokens/month? Also any amortized credit schedule?

Procurement is on copy; they may want the CSV attached to the SOW. If you can send a sample layout and draft rebate tiers, we can loop legal.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — we have a procurement sync on Friday.

Thanks,
Emma Liu
Head of Platform Integrations
CloudHarbor Inc.

Hi Emma — great to hear the pilot got useful signals. Short answers up front, details below and I attached a sample CSV layout and an initial rebate worksheet (Proposed_Rebate_Tiers_20270412.xlsx).

- We can deliver a token-level export (prompt vs completion) per model per day; format is CSV with columns: date, model, env (prod/staging), prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, billed_tokens, request_id (where available).
- For a 6-month commit we typically offer stepped rebates by committed monthly throughput. Example (ballpark): 0–5M tokens: $0.00040/token; 5–25M: $0.00032/token; 25M+: $0.00025/token. Final pricing depends on model mix (L/R family), and whether you want guaranteed latency SLOs.
- Credits/rebates are usually amortized monthly against invoices as a line-item credit; we can also apply an upfront credit and amortize it if you prefer (we'll show both options).

Next steps I propose: I’ll drop the CSV layout now, Marissa (cc’d) will propose formal tiers and legal language, and Neha (cc’d) can confirm how rebates will appear on invoices and what GL mappings we can provide. If procurement wants a DocuSign-ready SOW, we can produce that once tiers are agreed.

Attached: Proposed_Rebate_Tiers_20270412.xlsx (compact schedule), sample_usage_layout.csv (format only).

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Trial usage — request for itemized ledger and rebate mechanics

Hi Emma — adding a bit more color from pricing so you have a concrete starting point for procurement/legal. Sergio’s numbers are a solid baseline; here are two structured options we commonly use for trial-to-commit conversions: 

Option A — Volume rebate (simple, per-token):
- 6-month commit (monthly commit): tiered per-token pricing applied to actual billed tokens each month.
- Example tiers (for hosted API general models): 0–5M: $0.00040; 5–25M: $0.00030; 25M+: $0.00022.
- Credits applied monthly as a negative invoice line item titled "Commit Rebate". No upfront credit.

Option B — Upfront credit + performance kicker:
- Upfront non-refundable credit equal to X% of the first-month commit; monthly rebates applied if usage exceeds committed baseline.
- Kicker: additional 2–5% rebate if average request latency <= agreed SLO for the quarter.

Edge items:
- We break out token-level exports per model and include a model-family column (e.g., rtx-13b / rtx-70b).
- Overages: billed at a short-term overage rate (usually ~10–15% above the committed tier price) and then reconciled at month-end when rebates apply.

If you want, I can convert Option A into legal-ready contract language and attach a sample invoice line-item mock that maps to your GL. Sergio — can you confirm CloudHarbor needs per-endpoint breakdowns or per-model is sufficient?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions & GTM
Redwood Inference

Emma / team — I exported a sample CSV for April 1–10 to show exactly what we can deliver. Attached: CloudHarbor_Usage_Q2.csv (redacted customer_ids). The file includes: date, model_name, region, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, billed_tokens, request_id, route_id, project_tag.

A few finance notes: 
- Invoice presentation: line items will appear as "Usage — <model_name>" rows aggregated by month and then a separate "Commit Rebate" credit row that references the rebate agreement id. We can also add a memo field on the invoice that points to the HubSpot deal id for your internal reconciliation.
- Export flavors: we can provide (a) raw token-level CSV (as attached), (b) pre-aggregated monthly GL mapping CSV, or (c) a JSON export if your systems prefer.
- For accounting: rebates are applied as contra-revenue credits and amortized monthly. If you want an upfront credit amortized over 6 months we will label the invoice credits with the period they cover.

Attached: CloudHarbor_Usage_Q2.csv (sample).

2) For Option A above, confirm that overages are billed at the higher rate and then reconciled with the month-end rebate (i.e., customers don’t get double-billed).
3) On amortization: we prefer an upfront credit amortized monthly so the monthly invoices show predictable net spend. Please send a mock invoice (PDF) showing both the upfront credit amortized over six months and the "monthly rebate" approach so procurement can decide.

If you can deliver the CSV with the added column and the two mock invoice PDFs by Friday EOD I’ll route to legal. If not, propose a 30-minute slot — Friday 10:00–10:30 PT works for us.
